description: Colaba Woods is located near the President Hotel in South Mumbai. About 5 km from the CST railway station.[1] The Colaba woods garden is located on C.T.S. No. 87A and 88B. It is spread over 31,000 m2. It is a beautiful wooded tree garden near to high sky scraper buildings. In the early 190's the Tata Electric Company took over an eight-acre plot of land from the MCGM. This was called as Colaba woods. It was a refuse dump. Today this green forest in the concrete jungle at Cuffe Parade is the lung of the locality. It has several facilities like joggers' track, an amphi-theater, a readers' corner for street children, basketball courts, children play areas and areas for relaxation. Colaba Woods won the Urban Heritage Award in 1989.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellant place for Morning Walker, kids and families.

HERITAGE GARDEN: De-stressing and Rejuvenating in a Different World

Pramod Chavan

Surrounded by high-rise concrete buildings and glass-fronted skyscrapers opposite the Glen Towers on Cliff Avenue Road in Powai, a Heritage Garden means Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee Udyan is a de-stressing and rejuvenating world.

The special thing about this ten-acre park is that it is not just a park for one class or one age group. On one side are college students on the fence and on the other a group of senior citizens reminiscing. Here, among the youth the guitar tunes, and among the senior citizens, someone easily makes the flute tunes, mesmerizing the entire atmosphere.

Apart from the magnificence of the surrounding residential complexes, it is the right space for yoga enthusiasts with its many offices and commercial setups. It has become a place for those who practice regular and mixed martial arts.

The landscaped lawns, a separate play area for children, a Japanese-style Miyawaki patch on one side and a circular walking path that winds around the periphery of the park make the Heritage Garden a pleasant place to spend an evening with your loved ones.

Heritage Garden is one of the main places for morning walkers in Powai and the surrounding area. There is a beautiful gazebo apart from benches at regular intervals. It also has a beautiful artificial pond which often has beautiful lotus flowers.

The stone structure along the circular walkway attracts the attention of all new visitors. There is also a restroom on one side of the park.

Another special feature of this park is that some other parks in the city often organize events, so people coming to the park have a lot of trouble. However, events or other mass activities are still not allowed here without permission.

The man-made wells located at the corners of the park are used the most during monsoons. But it has not been able to escape from the habit of people coming to the garden to throw large amounts of waste.

Garden gates open at 5 am, after that they are closed from 12 noon to 4.30 pm... and open again from 4.30 pm to 10 pm.

Mumbai is a big mouthful that needs to be taken in small bites.
We, a Danish couple, were lucky to have a whole day with two highly qualified guides.

featured_reviews.name: Х. У. З.
featured_reviews.review_text: I called to book my tour the same morning and was happy that they were able to accommodate me last minute! Aamir was my guide for the slum and laundry tour - he clearly knew where he was going and what he was doing, and although I could tell he had walked the same route many times before, it didn’t feel touristy or artificial at all. It just felt like we were walking through a neighborhood he knew well, where more or less everything was open to the outside world. We started off in the area where there are many small factories for clothing, recycling, and bakery products - at every little business we encountered, he simply had to ask to enter, and we could walk right in and see the process up close. It was fascinating to me - I never would have imagined that the bread I buy in a supermarket or clothes I buy in a normal store come from such small-scale operations and not major, industrial manufacturing plants. We also passed through a residential area, and I even stopped to get henna done from a woman we met at random while inside her neighbor’s pottery studio. For that reason, we didn’t have a lot of time towards the end, and the laundry was just a stopover at the lookout over the area (where I was mobbed by vendors trying to sell me things; an expected part of being an outsider in India), but overall it felt like a very authentic look into the everyday lives of much of Mumbai’s lower class. I took a private tour so I wasn’t in a big group, and I’m not that much into taking photos so we moved very fast - which is what I preferred as there was so much to see. Highly recommended.

Rajabai Tower, University of Mumbai: The Mumbai University is undoubtedly one of the finest examples of Victorian Neo Gothic
Architecture in Mumbai. It is also an integral part of one of the finest urban ensembles of Victorian buildings in the world. The Rajabai Tower, with its imposing skyline, dominates the skyline of the Fort area, thus further strengthening its classification for reasons of scenic value.
The Mumbai University, designed by Sir Gilbert Scott, is an example of a public project in the city funded by local philanthropists, in this case, the "Cotton King" of Bombay, Premchund Roychund who made a generous contribution of Rupees 4 lakhs towards its construction. As a gesture of acknowledgment, the lofty Rajabai Tower, an awesome structure that rose to a height of 260 feet, was named after his mother. The Library structure adjoining the Rajabai Tower has among the finest ensembles of stained glass in the country while the splendid cross vaulted roof of the Reading Room with its polished timber members, is among the most spectacular architectural interiors in the city.

The 85-meter-tall tower is adorned with exquisite stained glass windows and intricate carvings, making it a treat for architecture enthusiasts. Named after Rajabai, the mother of its patron, Premchand Roychand, the tower is not only a testament to Mumbai's colonial heritage but also a functioning clock tower. featured_reviews.review_text:
Beautiful place which is seen from city
The 142-year-old Rajabai Clock Tower in South Mumbai’s Fort area, located inside University of Mumbai’s campus, is iconic for its Victorian-Gothic architecture. Built in 1878 by architect Sir George Gilbert Scott, it was commissioned by businessman Premchand Roychand as a tribute to his mother, hence the name. For years, it was the city’s tallest structure, at 285 feet. Rajabai Clock Tower has long been a beacon of the Oval Maidan precinct, a visual delight, and a valuable piece of history for the city. After brilliant restoration work by SNK Consultants, the clock tower was handed over to KSA Lighting Designers in 2017 for lighting the tower, the facade and the interiors of the University Library. Kanchan Puri, principal at the firm, tells us the process of this massive undertaking that was completed recently. After years of darkness, the Rajabai Clock Tower finally glowed up in 2021, literally.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nariman Point is one of those places in Mumbai that I've been visiting since childhood and it continues to hold the same sense of familiarity and quiet grandeur even today.

With every visit, whether during the day or late in the evening, it offers a slightly different experience, and I've had the chance to capture some beautiful views here over time.

What many may not be aware of is that Nariman Point is named after Khurshid Framji Nariman (Veer Nariman). He was a prominent Parsi who played an important role during India's freedom movement and was a powerhouse in the Civil Disobedience movement and a close associate of Sardar Patel. He was the Mayor of Bombay and a fearless critic of British corruption. Nariman Point stands today as a tribute to his legacy, not just as a landmark.

Today, Nariman Point is known for its sweeping sea views, clean promenade, and its proximity to some of Mumbai’s iconic landmarks, including the Trident Hotel, Oberoi and other prominent establishments that line this stretch. It is also the southern tip of the famous Marine Drive.

During the day, it offers a calm and open space to sit by the sea and unwind. By night, it transforms into one of the best vantage points to witness the iconic “Queen’s Necklace” which is the beautifully lit curve of Marine Drive.

The area is generally safe, well-patrolled, and frequented by both locals and visitors, making it a comfortable spot even for those new to the city.

With several dining options nearby and easy accessibility, Nariman Point remains a must-visit location in Mumbai. Be it for its views, its history, or simply the experience of being by the sea.

The Heart of Mumbai's Cricket and Heritage!

"Oval Maidan is a vast and vital green space in the Fort area, providing a much-needed open area in the busy South Mumbai.

It is most famous for its role in Mumbai's cricket scene, with countless matches being played simultaneously, especially on weekends.

It is a fantastic place to witness the city's passion for the sport.

The Maidan is bordered by stunning Victorian Gothic and Art Deco architecture, including the Bombay High Court and the University of Mumbai, which makes for a beautiful and historic backdrop.

It serves as an excellent spot for a morning run, an evening stroll, or just relaxing under the shade of a tree.

While it can get busy, the Oval Maidan is essential to the city's spirit and a perfect place to experience local life and admire Mumbai's rich architectural heritage."

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Occupying a majestic 22-acre expanse in the heart of South Mumbai,the Oval Maidan is a sublime palimpsest of colonial grandeur and contemporary leisure. Enveloped by the architectural duality of the Victorian Gothic revival to the east and the sleek Art Deco ensembles to the west now collectively enshrined as a UNESCO World Heritage site the ground serves as a verdant bridge between centuries.
To traverse its periphery is to witness a sophisticated choreography of Mumbai’s social fabric. Under the watchful shadow of the Rajabai Clock Tower, the air is thick with the rhythmic thwack of willow against leather, as aspiring cricketers populate the dusty pitches in a relentless pursuit of sporting excellence. The maidan functions as a civic lung, exhaling a serene tranquility that contrasts sharply with the frantic kinesis of nearby Churchgate.
The aesthetic appeal lies in its unmanicured authenticity; it is neither a rigid botanical garden nor a chaotic wasteland, but a curated void that permits the city to breathe. As the golden hour bathes the limestone gargoyles of the High Court in amber hues, the Maidan transcends its physical boundaries, becoming a temporal sanctuary. It is an indispensable urban theater where history remains a living, breathing participant in the everyday life of the metropolis. For the discerning visitor, it offers a peerless vantage point to observe the architectural and cultural heartbeat of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Amol Angwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, and it was a truly enriching experience.

The museum is beautifully maintained and offers a deep dive into India’s history, art, and culture. From ancient sculptures and artifacts to miniature paintings and decorative arts, every section is thoughtfully curated and informative. The building itself is stunning, with its grand Indo-Saracenic architecture adding to the overall charm of the visit.

One of the highlights is how well the exhibits are organized, making it easy to explore at your own pace. The descriptions are clear and help you understand the historical significance of each piece.

We also opted for the audio guide for our 9-year-old daughter, and it turned out to be a great decision. She found it very engaging, moving from one stop to another, listening to the stories and explanations with curiosity. It made the experience interactive for her and is a wonderful way for kids to learn about history in an enjoyable manner.

The premises are clean and well-managed, and the staff is helpful and courteous.

Overall, it’s a must-visit in Mumbai, perfect for both adults and children. I would recommend setting aside at least 2–3 hours to fully explore and appreciate everything the museum has to offer.

featured_reviews.name: Rishi Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya was an absolute highlight. The grand Indo-Saracenic building itself is a masterpiece, surrounded by beautifully maintained, peaceful gardens that offer a calm escape right in the middle of South Mumbai.

Inside, the collection is incredibly vast and well-organized. Walking through the different galleries—from the ancient Indus Valley artifacts and stunning stone sculptures to the miniature paintings and the natural history section—feels like traveling through time. Everything is beautifully displayed with clear information.

Time budget tip:
If you want to dive into all the deep historical details, expect to spend a solid 2 to 3 hours here. However, if you are short on time, you can easily do a brisk walkthrough in about 1-1.5 hours and still get a wonderful overall experience, just with a bit less detailed reading. It's an absolute must-visit for anyone wanting to experience India’s rich heritage!

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh K R
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya recently, and while the permanent collections are always impressive, what truly stood out this time were the special exhibitions currently on display—deeply immersive, contemporary, and culturally rooted.

The “Roots of a City: The Pathare Prabhus of Mumbai” exhibition is incredibly intimate. Instead of telling history through grand events, it brings together family heirlooms, photographs, recipes, and everyday objects to narrate the story of one of Mumbai’s oldest communities. It feels less like a museum display and more like stepping into someone’s living memory—quiet, layered, and deeply human.

The “Metamorphosis II” exhibition offers a striking contrast—more interpretive and artistic—exploring transformation through textiles, craft, and visual storytelling. The curation feels thoughtful and contemporary, making traditional practices feel alive and evolving rather than static.

I also really appreciated the installation work (including pieces like Navjot Altaf’s environmental/art narratives such as “Waste archives as Landscapes ”), which added a powerful social and ecological lens to the overall experience—pushing you to reflect, not just observe.

Overall, what makes CSMVS special right now is how it balances:History + personal memory,
Craft + contemporary interpretation, Heritage + social commentary

The museum itself, with its Indo-Saracenic architecture and vast collection of ~50,000 artefacts, remains one of Mumbai’s cultural anchors—but these exhibitions elevate it into something far more dynamic and relevant today.

If you’re in Mumbai, don’t just go for the main galleries—make time for the temporary exhibitions. They’re the real highlight right now.

featured_reviews.name: LeLe
featured_reviews.review_text: Highly recommend this outstanding tour! Friends of mine did a food tour with Arpan and liked it so much they booked a walking tour with him for the next day and asked me to join. Arpan took us to interesting places, some of which you wouldn't find in a tour guide and he knew a lot to tell about them, you get to meet locals and hardly see any other tourists. Arpan is super funny and smart, he speaks excellent English and has very reasonable prices for his tours. If I come back to Mumbai I'll definitely do a tour with him again.

featured_reviews.name: Sas Mac
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Mumbai as a solo female traveller in May 2019 with 2 nights booked not knowing anyone or much about the city. I saw Bombay walks advertised at my hostel and thought I would check it out for the evening to introduce me to the city. I ended up staying and extra night and booking a tour with Arpan everyday as I had so much fun and made my way around the city like a local on the trains, tuk tuks and walking. I ate street food and was shown the history of Mumbai. Arpan was fun, respectable and knowledgable about Mumbai and India. He gave me help with the rest of my trip, recomending Udaipur and booking my flights for my. He also has great insite into hostels throughout the country!

Great guy, couldn't recommend him more

featured_reviews.name: Sam Shapiro
featured_reviews.review_text: Arpan was great- he was very knowledgeable about the history of India and of the places he took us. He began by providing us with context for everywhere we were going to go that day, showing us on a map what the route would look like and why he chose the places he was taking us to. Each place he took us was very interesting and, as promised, slightly different than what you may find from a more generic tour. He was great at answering questions, and ended the tour with a discussion with the group about what it’s like to grow up in India.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.name: Moni K.
featured_reviews.review_text: Thanks to Bombay Walks Mumbay became the highlight of my India trip! Arpan took me to hidden places to give me an authentic insight to the city and its lifestyle and it was just amazing. I experienced street food, local markets and cozy bars with him. As a female solo traveller i never felt unsafe during my time with Arpan. He is such a perfect guide who speaks clear english and takes care of u all of the time. Really highly recommendable, also for female travellers!

featured_reviews.name: Tonya Lenox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Simply amazing. It was our last tour of our trip but easily our favorite one!  I wish he could’ve done all our tours through India! And such a good price.
He was our only tour guide who did not push us to purchase things or leave a review. He cared more about us truly having a good experience and understanding of his country.
He had a lot of knowledge of so many different aspects of not only the locations he showed us but also could answer a lot of questions we had about India in general as well. He was timely, communicated easily and most importantly had a great mix of fun and truth on the tour. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: sheena patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai, it’s a city I’ve ‘visited’ many times however I wouldn’t say I had experienced the localities until I booked myself on the fabulous walking tour with Arpan. Bombay walks allowed tourists to experience the pockets of the city in detail and depth.

Arpan is extremely knowledgable about the various different neighbourhoods of mumbai. The tour takes you through various areas of the crazy city. He will point out all the landmarks, highlights and he definitely knows some of mumbai’s best hidden coffee spots😉.

You can ask him a million questions and he will patiently give you all the answers.
Leaving you in awe of how Mumbai comes together chaotically.

The tour had been designed to give tourists like myself a taster of this metro. I would highly recommend it! Our bilingual Arpan can share his stories in English, Hindi, Marathi and Marwari :)

I look forward to returning to Mumbai soon  and participating in many other walks!

Would have not been able to experience the beautiful churches, streets, food and art of Bandra without his support. One should definately opt for this walking tour.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text: Gowalia Tank Maidan, officially renamed August Kranti Maidan, is a park in Grant Road West, in South Mumbai, in which Mahatma Gandhi issued the Quit India speech on 8 August 1942. The Maidan is now a popular playground. Cricket is the popular game although the monsoon season is primarily for football and volleyball. The ground has been split into 5 smaller grounds.
